venue: GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City

analysis.summary: Netherlands enter this dead rubber as heavy favourites having scored 7 goals in two Group F games (5-1 vs Sweden, 2-2 vs Japan) while sitting level on 4 points with Japan but leading on goal difference. Tunisia are already eliminated having conceded 9 goals in two matches (lost 1-5 to Sweden, 0-4 to Japan), had their manager Sabri Lamouchi sacked mid-tournament, and have no points to play for. Ronald Koeman's side have strong tactical motivation to win and secure Group F top spot, which would earn them a Round of 32 match against Morocco rather than Brazil.
analysis.home_form: Tunisia have been dismal at this World Cup: a 1-5 defeat to Sweden on Matchday 1 and a 0-4 loss to Japan on Matchday 2, conceding 9 goals with zero clean sheet potential. Their manager was dismissed after the Japan defeat. They scored only 1 goal across both matches (a consolation vs Sweden) and have shown severe defensive disorganisation.
analysis.away_form: Netherlands have been in outstanding attacking form: a 2-2 draw vs Japan (underperforming xG slightly) followed by a dominant 5-1 win over Sweden. Brian Brobbey scored twice vs Sweden, Cody Gakpo added two more. The Dutch have scored 7 goals in 2 games but have conceded 3, failing to keep a clean sheet in any of their last 6 matches. Memphis Depay is a doubt with a thigh problem; Brian Brobbey carries a minor knock but is expected to start.
analysis.h2h: Only three historical meetings: Netherlands won 4-0 in April 1978. The sides drew 2-2 in January 1994 and 1-1 in February 2009. This will be the first competitive fixture between the sides, so head-to-head history has limited predictive weight.
injuries_news: Brian Brobbey (Netherlands) carrying a knock from the Sweden game; fitness uncertain but expected to start.
Memphis Depay (Netherlands) working back from a thigh problem; unlikely to start but in the squad.
Quinten Timber (Netherlands) returned from concussion and is in contention.
No confirmed injury or suspension news for Tunisia key players.
key_factors: Netherlands have strong incentive to win: first place in Group F means facing Morocco (Group C runner-up) rather than Brazil (Group C winner) in the Round of 32.
Tunisia have conceded 9 goals in 2 games — the worst defensive record in their group — and have nothing to play for, suggesting minimal resistance.
Netherlands have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last 6 matches, meaning Tunisia may score via a set piece or error even against a heavily-rotated Dutch backline.
Koeman is expected to field near-full strength to secure top spot, making a dominant Dutch win the most likely outcome.
Kansas City's summer heat may reduce intensity in the second half, potentially limiting total goals below 5.
Group stage motivation gap: Netherlands motivated for seeding; Tunisia players competing for individual dignity only.
